decision: I approved the build with readiness 'ready_with_gaps'
I chose Node.js with Mongoose 7.x (pin to 7.7.0)
reason: Mongoose 7.x is widely compatible with MongoDB 7 wire protocol and matches the prompt review assumption; it keeps the sample simpler than introducing TypeScript or a newer major release with fewer tested docs in readiness report.
evidence: Assumption from prompt review: "Builder will use a modern Mongoose 7.x compatible with Node 24"

decision: I chose to read the connection string from environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI at runtime
alternatives: Read connection string from a config file
Read connection string from environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI
reason: It matches the readiness guidance, keeps secrets out of source, and is easiest for users to run the sample against an existing cluster.
evidence: Readiness report instruction: "Read DOCUMENTDB_URI at runtime from an environment variable in the sample (process.env.DOCUMENTDB_URI)"

decision: I chose not to provision resources; the sample uses the existing cluster and includes no provisioning actions
alternatives: Provision a cluster as part of the sample (Bicep/Terraform)
Do not provision — use existing cluster and provide IaC as files only
reason: Provisioning is disallowed by policy and the run environment already provides a reachable cluster; writing provisioning code would be unverified and possibly refused.
evidence: Run policy: "Azure resource changes allowed: False." and readiness report guidance that cluster is provided

decision: I chose to create a unique index on chargeEvents.idempotencyKey (unique:true) and also index customerId
alternatives: Partial unique index where idempotencyKey exists
No unique index, check in application logic
reason: A unique DB index is the most reliable way to prevent double-billing under concurrency; application-level checks alone are race-prone.
evidence: Readiness report instruction: "Enforce idempotency by creating a unique index on the idempotencyKey"

decision: I chose to create a TTL index on entitlement.expiresAt with expireAfterSeconds: 0
reason: Using an expiresAt canonical field and expireAfterSeconds:0 matches recommendations and allows immediate expiry when the UTC timestamp passes.
